entries.title: Judge the Cyber Apocalypse by the Data, Not the Headlines
entries.summary: Real-world cyber impact data presents a mixed picture less dire than technical indicators suggest. Whilst AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery and attack speed since April 2025, significant breaches, healthcare incidents, and average breach costs remain stable or declining. Ransomware payouts are down despite increased attacks. Some datasets show growth, but appear driven by broader definitions rather than genuine escalation.

entries.title: SpaceX sued by Oregon and Virginia over AI deepfake porn, Grok safety claims
entries.summary: Covers lawsuits filed against SpaceX by Oregon and Virginia over AI-generated deepfake pornography and claims regarding Grok's safety features.

entries.title: What Makes Catastrophic Incidents Different?
entries.summary: Examines distinguishing characteristics of catastrophic incidents compared to other disasters and their implications for emergency management preparedness.

entries.title: Norway links energy firm cyberattacks to critical Azure API Management flaw
entries.summary: Norway attributes cyberattacks on an energy firm to a critical Azure API Management flaw. Microsoft reports mitigations exist but administrators must investigate potential compromises and rotate secrets.

entries.title: Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years
entries.summary: Bulgarian government networks harboured intruders for five years who downloaded over 130 GB of data. Political instability reportedly contributed to security neglect enabling the breach.

entries.title: Everything going down at once wasn't evidence of a conspiracy – but the truth may be scarier
entries.summary: Recent widespread service outages revealed extensive technical debt rather than evidence of coordinated conspiracy by rogue AI or nation-state actors.

entries.title: Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September
entries.summary: Google reports a critical VMware bug was actively exploited weeks before public disclosure. China-linked ARMORY CASTLE deployed five custom malware tools against vCenter.

entries.title: Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX over Grok’s porn deepfakes
entries.summary: Oregon and Virginia filed separate lawsuits against SpaceX alleging violations of consumer protection laws by ignoring safeguards against AI-generated sexual deepfakes and misrepresenting X and Grok safety.

entries.title: The Double Alignment Problem: Civil-Military Relations in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
entries.summary: Artificial intelligence poses the greatest challenge to American civil-military relations since nuclear weapons. AI creates a dual alignment problem: aligning the state with the military, and aligning humans with AI agents. This threatens constitutional governance and military professionalism, yet civil-military relations scholarship lags far behind AI development.

entries.title: States Sue SpaceX Over Grok Deepfakes
entries.summary: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general are suing Elon Musk's companies, alleging they implemented inadequate safeguards against sexualised imagery of real people, including children.

entries.title: Google Wants To Make a 24/7 AI TV Channel. You’ll Be the Main Character
entries.summary: Google has patented a system called 'My Channel' that would generate 24/7 personalised AI television using user data, with viewers as protagonists. The system would insert targeted advertisements into AI-generated shows based on demographic information and viewing history.

entries.title: ‘The Code Is Already Copied Everywhere’: The AI Hacking Tool Causing Havoc Around the World
entries.summary: ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking framework, enables rapid automated cyberattacks targeting government, healthcare, telecommunications, legal, defence, financial and semiconductor sectors globally. Despite the creator removing it from GitHub, copies remain freely available. The FBI warns it can complete entire hacks in hours.

entries.title: Digital sovereignty not smart, says The Hague CIO
entries.summary: The Hague's CIO argues European digital sovereignty from US technology is unrealistic. Despite council demands for independence from American suppliers following ICC sanctions concerns, he maintains that complete separation from US tech providers is impractical.

entries.title: Nation-state APTs don't need new tricks; the old ones still work
entries.summary: Nation-state advanced persistent threats continue using established techniques like phishing and credential theft whilst adapting them to exploit newly adopted technologies. They demonstrate sophistication by identifying operational value in emerging technologies rather than developing entirely novel attack methods.

entries.title: UK Sovereign AI Fund invests in defence tech startup
entries.summary: UK government's Sovereign AI Fund and National Security Strategic Investment Fund invested in Agon, which develops infrastructure for training autonomous defence systems, including AI tools against drone attacks and a virtual battlefield for testing. The investment supports UK technological independence from overseas providers.

entries.title: Staff gagging clauses lifted for review of ‘toxic culture’ at information watchdog
entries.summary: Non-disclosure agreements with UK Information Commissioner's Office staff will be lifted to enable an independent review of culture and governance following the resignation of information commissioner John Edwards over sexual harassment and bullying allegations.

entries.title: A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
entries.summary: Philosopher Thomas Nagel has criticised Anthropic's position on AI consciousness. Anthropic considers AI sentience a risk factor and treats the possibility seriously, citing philosopher support. Nagel, whose work shaped consciousness theory, calls this approach idiotic, despite his own writing highlighting consciousness's subjective, unknowable nature.

entries.title: The Download: AI’s judgment problem and carbon removal’s crop threat
entries.summary: METR's updated AI evaluation report finds some capabilities improving exponentially, but models struggle with judgment-requiring tasks like designing evaluations and scoring arguments. Separately, research suggests enhanced rock weathering for carbon removal could reduce crop yields more than anticipated, potentially shrinking carbon removal potential.

entries.title: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya
entries.summary: Covers Ukraine's confirmed use of naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya.

entries.title: NATO believes Russia is ready to launch nuclear-armed satellite, German media say
entries.summary: Covers NATO's assessment that Russia is preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite, according to German media reports.
